la:noun:virtus.html:
virtūs, ūtis (
gen. plur. virtutium, ; ; dat. and abl. VIRTVTEI, Inscr. Corp. Lat. 1, 30 and 34), f.
vir
, manliness, manhood, i. e. the sum of all the corporeal or mental excellences of man, strength, vigor; bravery, courage; aptness, capacity; worth, excellence, virtue, etc.: virtus clara aeternaque habetur,: ni virtus fidesque vostra spectata mihi forent,; .
In gen.
Lit.: ita fiet, ut animi virtus corporis virtuti anteponatur,: his virtutibus ornatus, modestiā, temperantiā, justitiā,; cf.: virtutes continentiae, gravitatis, justitiae, fidei,: virtus atque integritas,: oratoris vis divina virtusque,.—
Transf., of animals, and of inanimate or abstract things, goodness, worth, value, power, strength, etc.: nam nec arboris, nec equi virtus (in quo abutimur nomine) in opinione sita est, sed in naturā,: praedium-solo bono, suā virtute valeat,: merci pretium statui, pro virtute ut veneat,: navium,: ferri,: herbarum,: oratoriae virtutes,: oratio habet virtutes tres,: dicendi (opp. vitium),: facundiae,.—
In partic.
In the phrase deūm virtute, usu. with dicam, by the aid or merit of the gods, i. e. the gods be thanked (anteclass), : virtute deūm et majorum nostrūm,; dub.; cf. and 90; so virtute eorum (i. e. majorum),.—
Moral perfection, virtuousness, virtue.
Lit.: est autem virtus nihil aliud quam in se perfecta et ad summum perducta natura,: virtus est animi habitus naturae modo rationi consentaneus,: cum omnes rectae animi affectiones virtutes appellentur ... Appellata est ex viro virtus, etc.,; : nec vero habere virtutem satis est quasi artem aliquam, nisi utare ... virtus in usu sui tota posita est,: est in eo virtus et probitas et summum officium summaque observantia,, a, 2.—
Transf., Virtue, personified as a deity, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —
Military talents, courage, valor, bravery, gallantry, fortitude (syn. fortitudo), etc.: Helvetii reliquos Gallos virtute praecedunt, quod fere cottidianis proeliis cum Germanis contendunt,; cf. ; 1, 13: militum,; : Claudi virtute Neronis Armenius cecidit,: Scipiadae,; cf. ; ; .—
Obstinacy: iniqua,.

senses: brave or courageous man, hero, warrior
la:noun:vir.html:
vĭr, vĭri (
gen. plur. virūm, Enn. ap. P., or Ann. v. 280 Vahl.; id. ap. Müll., or Ann. v. 394 Vahl.; ), m.
Sanscr. vira, hero; the root is in O. H. Germ. weralt; Angl.Sax. veruld; Engl. world, i. e. age or generation of men
, a male person, a man (opp. femina; cf. mas).
In gen.: virum me natam vellem,: deque viro factus (mirabile') femina,: ambiguus fuerit modo vir, modo femina Sithon,: mulier conjuncta viro,: vir mulierque,: sapientissimorum nostrae civitatis virorum disputatio,: vir prudens,: clari viri,: vir clarus et honoratus,: praestantior,: bonus et sapiens et legibus parens,; cf. ; v. bonus: optimi (opp. homines improbi),: fortis,; : turpissimus,: nefandus,.—
In partic.
A man as related to a woman, a husband, maritus (very freq.): is (Juppiter) amare occepit Alcumenam clam virum,; ; ; 1, 3, 4; : quem (vultum) dicitur Xanthippe praedicare solita in viro suo fuisse,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —Transf., of animals, the male, mate, etc., ; ; ; .—
A man (opp. a boy): pueri hoc possunt, viri non potuerunt?: ex toto non sic pueri ut viri curari debent,: pueroque viroque,: neque eos (pueros) prius in urbem redire, quam viri facti essent, statuit,: cum essem parvulus ... quando factus sum vir, etc.,.—
Pregn., a man, a man of courage, principle, or honor, one who deserves the name of a man: Marius rusticanus vir, sed plane vir, cum secaretur, vetuit se alligari ... Ita et tulit dolorem, ut vir; et, ut homo, majorem ferre sine causā necessariā noluit,; cf. : cum is jam se corroboravisset ac vir inter viros esset,: te oro, te colligas virumque praebeas,: si vir esse volet, praeclara συνοδία, : tum viro et gubernatore opus est,; ; ; 2, 38, 6 et saep.: si quid in Flacco viri est, Non feret,.—
In milit. lang.
In gen., like our man, for soldier (syn. miles): dispertiti viri, dispertiti ordines,; cf.: boat Caelum fremitu virum,: vir

unus cum viro congrediendo, T. Manlius, M. Valerius, quantum Gallicam rabiem vinceret Romana virtus, docuerunt, .—

In partic., as opposed to the cavalry, a foot-soldier (syn. pedes): equites virique,: magnā voce trahens equitemque virosque,: passim turmaeque virique, etc.,.—Hence, prov.: equis viris, or viris equisque, with horse and foot, i. e. with might and main; v. equus.—
With emphasis in place of a pronoun of reference, is, ille, etc.: fletusque et conploratio fregere tandem virum,: hae tantae viri virtutes,; .—
Distributively, each man, every man: vir virum legit, of choosing a senator,: vir cum viro congrediaris,: legitque virum vir, singled out (in battle), (an imitation of Hom. Il. 4, 472: ἀνὴρ δʼ ἄνδρʼ ἐδνοπάλιζεν): cum vir virum legisset,i. e. a companion in battle,; cf., in a sarcastic transfer-: ille (Clodius), qui semper secum scorta, semper exoletos, semper lupas ducebat, tum neminem, nisi ut virum a viro lectum esse diceres,.—
Human beings (poet. homines, opp. pecudes), ; cf. .—
Manhood, virility (poet. and very rare): ut relicta sensit sibi membra sine viro,: ferro mollita juventus Atque exsecta virum,.

la:adj:virilis.html:
vĭrīlis, e, adj.
vir
,
of or belonging to a man, manly, virile (cf.: mas, masculus).
Lit.
In respect of sex, male, masculine.
In gen.: virile et muliebre secus, ap. : virile secus, i. e. puer,: vestimentum,: genus,: semen,: stirps fratris,: vox,: vultus,: coetus,of men,; cf. balnea, Cato ap. : flamma,the love of a man,.—
In partic.
In mal. part.: pars,; cf. .—As subst.: vĭrī-lia, ĭum, n., = membrum virile, ; ; .— Comp.: qui viriliores videbantur,—
In gram., of the masculine gender, masculine: nomen,, §§ 21 and 30 Müll.; ; —
In respect of strength, vigor, etc., manly, full-grown, arrived at the years of manhood: conversis studiis aetas animusque virilis Quaerit opes, etc.,: ne forte seniles Mandentur juveni partes pueroque viriles,the parts of fullgrown men,: pars magna domus tuae morietur cum ad virilem aetatem venerit,: toga,assumed by Roman youth in their sixteenth year,; ; ; —Opp. to female garments: sumpsisti virilem togam quam statim muliebrem stolam reddidisti,.—
Transf., in jurid. lang., of or belonging to a person, that falls to a person or to each one in the division of inheritances: ut ex bonis ejus, qui, etc., virilis pars patrono debeatur, a proportionate part, an equal share with others, Gai : tota bona pro virilibus partibus ad liberos defuncti pertinere,: virilis,; ; so, virilis portio, pr.; 31, 1, 70, § 2; .—
Transf., in gen.
Virilis pars or portio, share, part, lot of a person: est aliqua mea pars virilis, quod ejus civitatis sum, quam ille claram reddidit,my part, my duty,: plus quam pars virilis postulat,, § 7: cum illius gloriae pars virilis apud omnes milites sit, etc.,: quem agrum miles pro parte virili manu cepisset, eum senex quoque vindicaret,: haec qui pro virili parte defendunt, optimates sunt,i. e. to the utmost of their ability, as far as in them lies,; so, pro virili parte,: pro parte virili,; Ov. Tr. 5, 11, 23: pro virili portione,; .—
In other connections (poet.): actoris partis chorus officiumque virile Defendat, Orell. ad loc. —
Trop., of quality, worthy of a man, manly, manful, firm, vigorous, bold, spirited, etc.: veretur quicquam aut facere aut loqui, quod parum virile videatur,: laterum inflexio fortis ac virilis,: inclinatio laterum,: acta illa res est animo virili, consilio puerili,; so, ingenium,: vis ingenii (with solida),: audacia,: oratio (with fortis),; so, compositio,: sermo,: ratio atque sententia,: neque enim oratorius iste, immo hercle ne virilis quidem cultus est,.—As subst.: vĭrīlia, ĭum, n., manly deeds, Dietsch.—Sup.: ALMIAE SABINAE MATRI VIRILISSIMAE, etc., Inscr. Grud. p. 148, n. 5.—Adv.: vĭrīlĭter, manfully, firmly, courageously (acc. to II.), ; ; ; .—Comp.,, ; .
